cost: For B request/result bytes, R unique replies and I items: encoding O(B), ordered result map O(B+R log R), retained state O(B+I+draft tokens). apply adds downstream gate and optional training/finish costs. u64 usage addition and usize indices lack overflow guards. USD is weighted tokens/1000000 times 0.5, f64 rounded; no elapsed-speed claim.
description: Prepared patch requests and historical reply envelopes feed the same Outcome patch gates as direct annotation. State persists model, effort, training paths, corpus target, ordered items/drafts and request index chunks. Blind preparation clears corpus/hints but retains drafts for comparison.
forward: prepare validates teacher model, requires patch flow, loads hints, chunks at batch_size>=1, encodes fixed/variable blocks and then writes requests before state. parse_results maps each nonblank JSON line to id and success Reply or error; duplicate ids overwrite. apply looks up chunk index strings, parses blind blocks or adds patch replies, then invokes finish. Missing/errored replies refuse all their chunk items.
inverse: The preimage of a result map includes any blank lines, any overwritten earlier duplicate ids, and arbitrary discarded thinking blocks; final occurrences must decode to the observed Reply/errors. State roundtrip recovers serialized fields, not external files or teacher execution. Cost alone has many usage/model antecedents.
limitations: No prepare/apply/blind end-to-end fixture; optional training, corpus append and external teacher are unexecuted.
No corrupt State index/panic or numeric overflow injection.
state: With valid unique item ids, complete matching drafts and in-range chunks, request k refers to exactly that chunk. Parsing skips thinking blocks and preserves text-block concatenation order. These assumptions are unchecked on deserialized State; indexing can panic. The two preparation writes are not atomic together.
